account: Viz.ai of San Francisco submitted Viz HCM, machine learning software that reads a 12-lead ECG and flags signs associated with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy so that the patient can be referred for follow-up. FDA reviewers describe a retrospective study of 3,196 ECGs, 291 from patients with the disease and 2,905 from patients without it. The ECGs came from two hospitals in the Boston area and one in Salem, Massachusetts, and were recorded between 1 July 2017 and 30 June 2022. A cardiologist confirmed each label by review of the chart and any imaging. The software had a sensitivity of 68.4% and a specificity of 99.1%. At a disease prevalence of 0.2%, its positive predictive value was 13.7%. FDA granted the De Novo request on 3 August 2023 and found that the probable benefits outweigh the probable risks. The reviewers write that the benefit is added detection of a disease that is uncommon and difficult to diagnose. The study used historical records, so the software did not guide care, and it missed about one in three patients with the disease.
